impact.title: Impact & Evidence
impact.lede: China Pilot evidence and Global Advisor metrics are reported separately. They are not combined into one number.
impact.s1.label: 01 · China Pilot
impact.china.headline: 50+ internal-test participants
impact.china.body: Limited internal testing only. The China pilot was tested with more than 50 participants, including students from my school and a small number of farmers and village committee staff from communities in Hebei. It has not been publicly released, so these figures should be interpreted as early, exploratory evidence rather than public-user statistics.
impact.s2.label: 02 · Global Advisor
impact.global.headline: Global metrics have not started collecting yet.
impact.global.noticeBody: No site visit or feedback data has been recorded for the Global Advisor yet, so no number is published below. Each metric is defined here first, so that whatever appears later can be checked against its definition.
impact.metric.visits.name: Global site visits
impact.metric.feedback.name: Global feedback responses
impact.metric.understand.name: Helped understand options
impact.metric.ai.name: AI helpfulness
impact.metric.visits.def: Recorded website visits, not verified unique individuals.
impact.metric.feedback.def: Optional anonymous feedback submissions from people who chose to answer.
impact.metric.understand.def: Share of feedback respondents who rated this 4 or 5 out of 5. Blank answers are excluded from the denominator.
impact.metric.ai.def: Average of numeric 1–5 ratings only. “I did not use the AI analysis” and blank answers are excluded.
impact.table.caption: Global Advisor metric definitions
impact.table.note: Period covered and last updated will be filled in once collection begins. Until then these cells stay empty rather than showing an example number.
impact.s3.label: 03 · What these numbers mean
impact.meaning.headline: Read each number for exactly what it counts.
impact.meaning.chinaBody: The China pilot was conducted as limited internal testing with students and participants from several Hebei village communities and was not publicly released. Internal-test participants are not public users.
impact.meaning.visitsBody: Global site visits represent recorded website visits, not verified unique individuals.
impact.meaning.feedbackBody: Feedback is anonymous and optional. Any percentage on this page describes feedback respondents, not all website visitors.
impact.s4.label: 04 · Methodology note
impact.method.headline: How these figures are defined and updated
impact.method.definitionBody: Every public metric states what is being counted, where it comes from, what period it covers, and when it was last updated.
impact.method.sampleBody: China Pilot: more than 50 internal-test participants. Global Advisor: no feedback responses have been recorded, so no average and no percentage is published.
impact.method.updatedBody: Collection of Global Advisor metrics has not started, so there is no update date to report yet.
impact.method.anonymousBody: Feedback is anonymous and optional. No name, email, phone, address, IP address or browser fingerprint is collected.
impact.method.exploratoryBody: Early and exploratory evidence. These figures should be interpreted as early, exploratory evidence rather than public-user statistics.
impact.method.rule1: Counts start from the real recorded data. No baseline number is added to make a figure look larger.
impact.method.rule2: Free-text feedback is never published automatically. An anonymous quotation can only appear after manual review.
impact.method.rule3: Impact data follows the same traceability principle as the scoring: every published number must be traceable to its source.
impact.footMeta: Anonymous · Optional feedback · Early exploratory data
story.hero.heading: From cleaner skies to a harder question at home.
story.hero.body: I started this project with a simple question: when cleaner-energy transitions change how families heat and cool their homes, who helps ordinary households understand what actually fits their climate, budget, and living conditions?
story.hero.supporting: From a household-energy study in northern China to a global climate-adaptation decision tool.
story.hero.byline: A student-led climate and household energy project.
story.hero.imageAlt: Rooftop solar array on a building photographed for the project
story.s01.heading: Cleaner air can be a success. The transition can still be difficult at home.
story.s01.body: Energy transitions are often measured through emissions, infrastructure and policy. But households experience them through everyday questions: How much will this cost? Will the home stay warm in winter or cool in summer? How difficult is installation? What happens when a family does not know which technologies are available?
story.s01.pullQuote: A climate solution also has to make sense at the household level.
story.s01.labels: Cost · Climate resilience · Household constraints · Access to information
story.s01.imageAlt: Smart gas meter (NB-IoT) on a brick wall
story.s02.heading: One question became a pilot, and the pilot became a broader tool.
story.s02.t1.label: RESEARCH
story.s02.t1.body: I began by studying how household heating transitions can create different experiences for policy, climate outcomes and household well-being.
story.s02.t2.label: CHINA PILOT
story.s02.t2.body: I then developed an interactive China pilot to explore how people understand household heating choices and their trade-offs.
story.s02.evidence.headline: 50+ internal-test participants
story.s02.evidence.body: Limited internal testing with students from my school and a small number of farmers and village committee staff from communities in Hebei. The China pilot has not been publicly released.
story.s02.t3.label: GLOBAL ADVISOR
story.s02.t3.body: The next step was to expand the question beyond one region and beyond heating alone: What happens when climate, household income, cooling needs, installation constraints and different technologies all have to be considered together?
story.s02.t4.label: NOW
story.s02.t4.body: The result is the Climate Adaptation Energy Advisor: a tool where deterministic rules calculate the ranking and AI helps people understand what the results mean.
story.s02.imageAlt: Screenshot of the China Pilot welcome screen
story.s03.heading: The score comes from the data. The explanation comes from AI.
story.s03.step1.title: YOUR HOME
story.s03.step1.body: The tool starts with what matters to the household: income, home size, energy bills, heating and cooling needs, and practical home conditions.
story.s03.step2.title: LOCAL PUBLIC DATA
story.s03.step2.body: It combines those answers with traceable public data for the user's location, such as climate, energy prices and emissions factors.
story.s03.step3.title: DETERMINISTIC SCORING
story.s03.step3.body: Eligible paths are compared through transparent formulas for affordability, climate resilience, environmental impact and practicality.
story.s03.step4.title: AI EXPLANATION
story.s03.step4.body: AI explains the existing scores in plain language. It does not calculate, change or reorder the results.
story.s03.flow: User answers + local public data → deterministic scoring → AI explanation
story.s04.heading: What we are learning so far
story.s04.metric1.label: China pilot internal-test participants
story.s04.metric2.label: Global site visits
story.s04.metric3.label: Global feedback responses
story.s04.metric4.label: said the tool helped them better understand their options
story.s04.disclaimer: Early and exploratory evidence. The China pilot was conducted as limited internal testing with students and participants from several Hebei village communities and was not publicly released. Global site visits represent recorded website visits, not verified unique individuals.
story.s05.heading: Built from a student question
story.s05.body: I initiated the research question and led the project from the early study and China pilot through the design of the global advisor. My work has included project design, research, participant recruitment, analysis, product direction and the development of the decision framework. Also Listen to the opinions of industry insiders and feedbacks from users; collaborated with others during the process to refine the website model
story.s06.heading: There is no single best technology for every household.
story.s06.body: The next goal is not to tell every family to choose the same solution. It is to make complex household energy choices easier to understand across different climates, incomes and homes.
story.s06.d1.label: MORE PLACES
story.s06.d1.body: Expand reliable local public data to more countries and regions.
story.s06.d2.label: MORE HOUSEHOLDS
story.s06.d2.body: Learn from a wider range of households, including people with tighter budgets or fewer local energy choices.
story.s06.d3.label: BETTER EVIDENCE
story.s06.d3.body: Use real user feedback to improve the questions, scoring transparency and explanations.
